intro: Paramedics bring calm judgment, coordination and patient care to every call. The closest of the 25 careers below are Acute Care Nurses at an 85% match and Respiratory Therapists at 84%; respiratory therapists earn a BLS May 2025 median of $82,280, which is 36% more than the $60,600 paramedics earn.
why_it_works: On a call you assess a patient fast, coordinate with a partner and explain what is happening to frightened families. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.88 out of 5 for paramedics and coordination at 3.75. Nursing, respiratory therapy and surgical support use the same skills in a hospital setting. Some of these need a bachelor's degree. New skills include quality checks and evaluating systems.
tips: Ask nursing programs about bridge options for paramedics; many give credit for your training.
Respiratory therapy is the shortest step up in pay among the top matches and needs no degree beyond what you have.
Surgical Assistants earn $66,800, which is 10% more, and use your clinical experience in a steadier schedule.

faq.q: What jobs can former paramedics do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Acute Care Nurses (85%), Critical Care Nurses (84%) and Respiratory Therapists (84%), based on O*NET 31.0. Registered Nurses are also 82% matched and earn $97,550, which is 61% more than the paramedic median, though they usually need a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Which careers for paramedics pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more than $60,600. Radiation Therapists earn $105,310 (74% more), Registered Nurses $97,550 (61% more) and Detectives and Criminal Investigators $93,790 (55% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Acute and critical care nurses share the $97,550 nursing figure.

faq.q: Do paramedics need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: Often not. 21 of the 25 matches need no more education than paramedics already have, though only 6 of the top 10 do. Nursing roles usually need a bachelor's degree, held by 57% of workers in the closest match, and bridge programs can shorten that path.

The skills that most often need work are quality control analysis, operations analysis, systems evaluation and equipment selection. Social perceptiveness already rates 3.75 out of 5 for paramedics in O*NET, so the step is mostly technical and clinical depth.
